title: Light as particles: the photoelectric effect
description: Einstein's photons explain why a dim violet lamp frees electrons from a metal when a bright red lamp cannot, and the stopping voltage gives Planck's constant.

sources.title: Photoelectric effect (Wikipedia): Hertz 1887, Lenard 1902, Einstein 1905, Millikan 1914–1916
The Nobel Prize in Physics 1921: Albert Einstein (prize motivation; awarded in 1922)
Albert Einstein (Wikipedia): born in Ulm 1879, the Swiss patent office in Bern, 1905 papers
Annus mirabilis papers (Wikipedia): light-quantum paper received 18 March 1905 by Annalen der Physik
Max Planck (Wikipedia): 14 December 1900, his view of light quanta, Nobel Prize for 1918
Robert Andrews Millikan (Wikipedia): photoelectric tests 1914–1916, 1916 determination of h, Nobel Prize 1923
Planck constant (Wikipedia): exact SI value h = 6.62607015 · 10⁻³⁴ J·s since 2019
sources.note: The elementary charge $e = 1.602176634 \cdot 10^{-19}\ \text{C}$ is also exact in the SI since 2019.

sources.title: Work function (Wikipedia): table of work functions of the elements
sources.note: Tables differ by some tenths of an electronvolt (sodium 2.36 eV in many textbooks, 2.75 eV in this table): the value depends on the surface. The unit uses typical textbook values.

sources.title: Fotoni material bank, University of Helsinki (photoelectric effect and Planck's constant)
